name: South Mumbai Heritage Walk by MDT
description:
The Mumbai Heritage Walk is a great way to experience the city’s vibrant culture and rich history.
Mumbai Heritage Walk is probably known as the ‘dream city’ and rightly so the city is indeed like a beautiful, magnificent dream. Old Mumbai is the part of Mumbai that represents its heritage and history. Reflecting on the time of Colonial era, the area is studded with numerous tourist attractions. From Chhatrapati Shivaji terminus to the ‘White town’ to the University library to the magnificent Marine drive, the city has so many spectacular attractions that one can never miss. Explore all these places of Old Mumbai and many more with this heritage walk tour.

Walking tours expose many residents and visitors to the structures.

featured_reviews.review_text:
Juhu Beach is undoubtedly one of Mumbai's popular tourist destinations, but tucked away from the bustling crowds lies a hidden gem, Beach Walk Park. As an avid nature enthusiast and seeker of peaceful solace, my recent visit to this serene park left me thoroughly enchanted.

Beach Walk Park offers an idyllic retreat from the chaos of city life. Nestled on the edge of Juhu Beach, it provides a refreshing respite and an opportunity to connect with nature. The park's beautifully landscaped gardens, manicured lawns, and a serene ambiance instantly transport visitors to a tranquil oasis.

Upon entering, one is greeted with clean walkways and well-maintained greenery that stretches towards the horizon, evoking a sense of peace. Compared to other crowded spots in Juhu, this park offers a more secluded and relaxed environment, making it a perfect spot for leisurely strolls or a picnic with loved ones.

The park's main attraction is undoubtedly its picturesque view of the Arabian Sea. The sight of waves crashing against the shore while the sun casts its golden glow on the water is truly captivating. I found myself spending hours on the shoreline, indulging in the breathtaking scenery and the calming sound of waves. It is a haven for photography enthusiasts and nature lovers alike.

What sets Beach Walk Park apart is its well-maintained cleanliness and hygiene. The park staff diligently ensures that the premises remain litter-free, allowing visitors to fully immerse themselves in the natural ambiance. The presence of clean restrooms and seating areas adds to the convenience and comfort of visitors.

Additionally, the park boasts various recreational facilities, including a children's play area and fitness equipment for both adults and elderly visitors. These amenities make it an ideal destination for families to spend quality time together, enjoying the outdoors and engaging in activities.

One cannot ignore the convenient location of Beach Walk Park. Situated in the heart of Juhu, it is easily accessible, making it a popular spot among locals and tourists alike. Its proximity to nearby eateries and cafes adds to the overall appeal, allowing visitors to indulge in a satisfying meal or a refreshing beverage after a day of relaxation.

In conclusion, Beach Walk Park in Juhu provides a captivating escape from the frenetic pace of Mumbai. Its pristine setting, combined with breathtaking views, make it a soul-soothing retreat. Whether you seek tranquility, a romantic sunset, or a fun-filled day with family, this park offers it all. Visiting Beach Walk Park will undoubtedly leave you replenished, rejuvenated, and longing to experience its allure again.

featured_reviews.name: Shakeel Ahmed
featured_reviews.review_text:
When u walk along a promenade, distance covered is not important. Important is night colors capture along the Bay of Mahim shore in 1.25 km stretch. BWSL Promenede is a place placed beautifully on the way joining Western Mumbai to Southern Mumbai through magnificent Bandra Worli Sea Link (BWSL). While going to South Mumbai in morning or evening, just take a detour down below on left side before BWSL toll gate n u will be at Promenede on right side adjacent to Asha Bhosle Sargam Udyan. The promenade park opens/ closes at 06-09 a.m. n 05-09 p.m.
Attractive for Joggers, Runners, kids, elderly ppl, romantic couple, broken hearts n photo enthusiasts equally which I m proving thru pics. In this two level park stretch, there r three children parks of different age kids, four animals statues,  two public gyms. two amphitheaters, one basket ball court, uncountable romance sheds n endless retention wall n yes- no toilets.
There r two Balconies protruded in sea, beautiful dates tree witnessing dating couples on retention walls, park curves n geometry, artificial lit trees, beautiful imperial design poles of solar street lightings.
Found this park most beautiful in nights, especially at low tide times when u can see muddy land in various shapes representing a different natural profile in the sea from Meethi River Eastern side. And in the residual waters, beautiful light reflections in sea of Mahim- Dadar-Prabhadevi-Worli side high rise buildings lights.
Don't forget to see marvellous lighting decorations in this promenede from Christmas to Sankranti festival in mid January, which takes this already beautiful park to a totally different level.

featured_reviews.name: Derishta Pillay
featured_reviews.review_text:
At the outset I must say that neither myself nor my husband are huge fans of the usual guided walking tours mainly because we hate being taken to cliched and crowded tourist hotspots, listening to facts straight from the Wikipedia page and jostling for space with other tourists just to return sunburned and underwhelmed. In addition we'd already spent a hectic 5 weeks in India - we were tired, grumpy, waiting to fly back home and not at all looking forward to our last 4 days in Mumbai at all. So basically when our travel companions insisted we book a tour - the scene was set for disaster...
'Bombay Walks' single handedly turned this around and Mumbai actually turned out to be the highlight of our trip! (Nope this is not a sponsored review 😂)

The tour: Arpan's tour extends to the days before and after the actual tour as he offers valuable advice about where to stay/eat/party/shop etc. He speaks perfect English, is pleasant and very easy to communicate with. His passion and love for the city is infectious and you will end his tour enthralled, overwhelmed and completely charmed by Mumbai and it's people - vowing to come back and dig deeper, spend longer and see more. The city tour covers many facets of the city - traveling to hidden gems and local landmarks across the length and breadth of Mumbai. You get to see and experience aspects of Mumbai that you'd never be able to do alone with a guide book or google maps - like traveling on local trains and walking through Worli fishing village and stopping by at small off-the-beaten path temples and churches.

The guide: Arpan is reliable, trustworthy and comes well prepared for the type of group. His talking style is light-hearted and easy going but still knowledgeable and always engaging. He's the type of guide that can tell you interesting facts about the history, architecture and politics of a place but also where to get the best coconut water along the way and which public toilets are ok to use.
We only met Arpan in person on the day of the tour and although we were constantly bombarded with sights, sounds and smells (it is Mumbai after all) - it never once felt like we were just being dragged from point to point whilst he rattled off information but rather that we were spending the day walking around with an old friend.

Target travelers: We're fairly well travelled and yet this is the first time we've ever bothered to leave a tour review - on any platform - I think that in itself indicates how highly we recommend this tour.
This is really a 'must do' in Mumbai.
It's so good we would do this tour again even if it were to cover the exact route we already took. The walking wasn't particular strenuous so it's recommended for any age group it should also be noted that we found that     Arpan was discreetly always conscious of where the group members were and their safety and constantly aware of our surroundings and the locals around us - on that note I would recommend this tour even if you're a single female traveling alone.

When to do it: Try and do this tour on your first full day in Mumbai because it's also a great way to orientate yourself around the city and plan the rest of your time there.

That city that everyone talks about - that's all of India's many faces and layers in one, that accepts everyone, that's everyone's home - regardless of language, religion or creed - Mumbai is THAT city and you'd be crazy if you miss the opportunity to let a born-and-bred local guide you around...

featured_reviews.name: Liviu-Alexandru Buftea (Style)
featured_reviews.review_text:
If you found this place, you had a good guide!

I thought it was Portuguese, but it's actually British. Black as the basaltic rock that rises from the sea, Worli Fort gives a great overview of the bay and the city. It features the classic crenelations and ramparts of the 17th century, and guards the golf from the tip of this tongue of land.

The fort now is not officially maintained or "open to the public". In fact, it seems even locals don’t know about it, but my friend brought me here cause she heard it’s nice. It is accessible for explorer types, and is basically left abandoned.

The fort is simply used by people in this neighborhood for storage, hang out, kids play space, etc. Some clothes left out to dry on the sides, and some barrels and stuff in the rooms below.

Here we met a couple of guys from the city, chilling, listening to cool music, they welcomed us to chat.

It smelled of sea salt, soap, garbage, fish and rats, and the breeze brought “fresh” air from the sea.

As a first time visitor in India, I was in culture shock. Seeing everything was kind of like a dreamy, surreal landscape. So I probably romanticized it too much, for the place is a slum surrounded by a garbage dump, and people here have little chance to better their days, but they were happy, kind and curious.

It was an interesting and humbling experience, worth respect.

featured_reviews.review_text:
we did the essential Mumbai tour with Parvez. he was a great guide for a great trip. The tour started off near the Asiatic society, and we walked around the area originally inside the Fort walls. He helped create a wonderful imagery of what the city looked like when it was founded along with some stories about the history before hand that led up to establishing Mumbai.
The trip was a mixture of walking and getting in and out of a car to see various sites around the city. It was quite varied and allowed us to see some unusual sites we would not have seen by ourselves.
at the end of the tour, we stopped at a restaurant with Parvez and tried several dishes that were excellent. Common food that is regularly served in restaurants, but this was delicious.

If this was representative of the companies tou, I would strongly recommend them for a tour.

featured_reviews.name: Varun Khandka
featured_reviews.review_text:
This afternoon we went for a heritage walk of the BMC office. We randomly signed up for this, thought its better to do something rather than just sitting home, but this was so much more than just "something".
We met Mr. Mickey, who led the walk, such an amazing, lively and knowledgeable guy. He kept the whole walk so engaging, the way he explained us about the things was truly outstanding. This was one of the best things to experience in Mumbai, we have already planned to do the fort walk and we are definitely going to sign up for more with Khaki Tours.

featured_reviews.name: Chirag
featured_reviews.review_text:
Must do -- even if you are a local!

We have been to the Fort area multiple times and while we have driven past the monuments multiple times, we never observed them!

Walking tour with Khakhi, helped us see the details that we have never noticed, heard stories that we did not know and helped us appreciate the history behind the buildings.

Our tour guide (Omkar) was very patient (especially with our 9 year old) and knowledgeable. He gave us a detailed tour and explained the nuances.

I would highly recommend this tour to anyone who wants to know about the history of Mumbai

featured_reviews.name: Sandy D
featured_reviews.review_text:
Did the Essential Mumbai tour with Sagar Joshi from Khaki Tours, and he was an excellent guide, storyteller, and truly passionate about Mumbai.

It was brutally hot the day we took the tour, but Sagar was patient, engaging, and took the time to explain everything in detail. Highly recommended for anyone wanting to experience and understand Mumbai beyond the usual tourist spots.

featured_reviews.name: Tejal Samant
featured_reviews.review_text: We visited the BMC Headquarters with Khaki Tours on 25th May, and it was an absolutely awesome experience! The heritage architecture of the building is simply stunning — a true gem in the heart of Mumbai. Every Mumbaikar should and must visit this iconic place to appreciate the city's rich history and civic pride. Our tour guide, Juzer Tambawalla, was incredibly knowledgeable and engaging, bringing the stories of this magnificent structure to life. Highly recommended!

featured_reviews.name: P K
featured_reviews.review_text: We had arranged for a group tour of Castle 2 Gateway through Khakee Tour. It was the best experience we ever had. We had 55 people in group most of them born and bought up in Mumbai. But we didnt knew even 10% history and facts of what they showed and explained us. We had 3 sub groups but everybody had excellent experience with their guides. Our tour guide was Parag who was fabulous. His passion for Mumbai was evident. A must do tour for every mumbaikar

featured_reviews.name: Max Mackie
featured_reviews.review_text:
Mumbai history comes alive! An amazing walk with Surabhi.

I recently took the Fort area heritage walk with Khaki Tours, and I cannot recommend it enough. Our guide, Surabhi, was absolutely fantastic.
It wasn’t just a recitation of dates and facts; Surabhi is a natural storyteller. She wove together the history of colonial Bombay with fascinating anecdotes about the architecture and the people who built this city. She pointed out hidden details in the Gothic buildings that I would have walked right past without noticing.

Her energy was contagious, and she was incredibly patient in answering all our questions. Whether you are a tourist or a local Mumbaikar, you will see the Fort area with completely new eyes after this. If you book a Khaki Tour, definitely ask for Surabhi!

featured_reviews.name: Sarvesh Salunkhe
featured_reviews.review_text:
Visited Veermata Jijabai Bhosale Udyan and Zoo (Rani Chi Baug) recently. The zoo is a good place for a family outing and children can enjoy seeing various animals and birds. The garden area is green and peaceful, making it suitable for a short walk.

However, some sections could be better maintained, and a few animal enclosures appeared smaller than expected. Due to crowds, especially on weekends, the overall experience can feel a bit rushed. Facilities and signboards could also be improved for visitors.

Overall, it’s a decent place to spend a few hours in Mumbai, particularly for families with kids, but there is room for improvement.

featured_reviews.name: ameya mahadik
featured_reviews.review_text:
Had a fantastic visit to Veermata Jijabai Bhosale Botanical Udyan and Zoo. The place offers a perfect blend of nature, history, and wildlife. The botanical garden is lush, well-maintained, and home to a wide variety of trees and plants, making it a refreshing escape in the heart of Mumbai.

The zoo is equally impressive, with a good collection of animals including tigers, hippopotamuses, crocodiles, deer, and many other species. The biggest attraction for me was the penguin enclosure. Seeing penguins up close was a unique experience and one of the major highlights of the visit.

The premises are clean, the animal enclosures are well organized, and there is plenty of information available for visitors. It's a great destination for families, children, wildlife enthusiasts, and anyone looking to spend a day surrounded by nature.

Overall, it was an enjoyable and memorable experience, and I would highly recommend visiting if you're in Mumbai.

featured_reviews.name: Rehan Shaikh
featured_reviews.review_text:
⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

Had a great experience at Rani Bagh. The zoo is clean, well-maintained, and surrounded by beautiful greenery. There is a good variety of animals and birds, making the visit both enjoyable and interesting. The atmosphere is peaceful, and it is a wonderful place to spend time with family and friends. Overall, a very pleasant and memorable visit. Highly recommended!

featured_reviews.name: Rohit Parui
featured_reviews.review_text: I absolutely love Veermata Jijabai Bhosale Botanical Udyan and Zoo. I highly recommend everyone to go and spend some quality time here with friends, family, and kids. It is a wonderful place where you can see a rich variety of different birds, animals, and beautiful trees. Beyond just being a fun day out, it is incredibly educational for kids as they can easily gain a lot of knowledge about nature and wildlife while exploring the beautiful grounds..

featured_reviews.name: Abir Khan
featured_reviews.review_text:
The place is well-maintained, but it feels more like a garden than a proper zoo due to the limited number of animals. There is only one tiger and one leopard, and several key animals are missing—there are no elephants, lions, or giraffes. The bird section also has very few species, although penguins are available, which is a plus.

The area is clean and spacious, and the food options inside are good. However, basic facilities like access to cold drinking water should be improved. Considering the large number of visitors and the strong revenue potential, the management should focus on adding more animals and enhancing overall maintenance to make the experience more worthwhile.

featured_reviews.name: Uday Pasupuleti
featured_reviews.review_text: Veermata Jijabai Bhosale Botanical Garden and Zoo is a wonderful attraction in Mumbai, combining beautiful greenery with an exciting wildlife experience. The garden is well maintained with lush landscapes, rare plants, and majestic old trees that make every walk refreshing. The zoo's major attractions include the penguins, Bengal tiger, leopard,Hippo,Bear, crocodiles, monkeys, deer, and a variety of colorful birds. Watching the penguins is especially a delight for both children and adults. The entire facility is clean, organized, and educational, making it an ideal destination for families, nature lovers, and photographers. A must-visit place to enjoy nature and wildlife in the heart of Mumbai

featured_reviews.name: Sana Pathan
featured_reviews.review_text: Lovely for a family visit especially with small kids. Good to see water fountains all around and decently maintained animal shelters... the children park is a good size albeit with quite a few swings broken and not well maintained... look into that please so kids can have thier share if fun

featured_reviews.name: Aditee Kale
featured_reviews.review_text:
VeerMata Jijabai Bhosale Udyan is a perfect place to visit for an enjoyable zoo experience in Mumbai. The zoo is well-maintained and offers a chance to see a wide variety of animals in a pleasant and engaging environment.

It houses animals such as tigers, leopards, sambar deer, barking deer, turtles, tortoises, and many more providing a great learning and viewing experience for visitors of all ages. There is also a dedicated bird park with multiple species of birds, including parrots and other colorful varieties, which is especially delightful. Everywhere there are information boards talking about that specific animal or bird, which becomes helpful for people to know what they are and what are the special / interesting facts about them.

One of the major attractions is the separate, temperature-controlled enclosure for penguins, which is very well designed and adds to the uniqueness of the zoo.

Additionally, the zoo has an in-house canteen that serves good food with a variety of options, including Indian and Chinese cuisine, juices, and chaat, making it convenient for visitors to relax and refuel during their visit.

Overall, it is a great place to spend quality time with family, kids and enjoy a refreshing day close to nature.

featured_reviews.name: Darren DSouza
featured_reviews.review_text:
The long promenade, sea breeze, and open space make it perfect for evening walks. There’s plenty of seating, play areas for kids, skating spots, and it’s also great for jogging.

There are restaurants and cafes nearby too, which makes it easy to spend a couple of hours here without feeling rushed. Definitely one of a refreshing spots in the city.

featured_reviews.name: Aniket
featured_reviews.review_text: Carter Road Promenade in Bandra is a beautiful seaside escape and one of Mumbai’s most loved walking spots. The long, well-laid promenade runs alongside the sea, offering stunning sunset views and a calming breeze, especially in the evenings. It is generally quite clean and well maintained, with plenty of benches to sit and relax while enjoying the view. Weekends can get crowded with walkers, joggers, families, and pet owners, but the vibe remains pleasant. Thankfully, there are no hawkers disturbing the space. However, the area seriously needs more decent, clean public toilets to improve the overall experience.

featured_reviews.name: Karan Shetty
featured_reviews.review_text:
They’ve added a section for skate park and boards. Kids and youngsters and skate enthusiasts seem to love it. I think it could do more good with a little more upkeep from authorities.

They’ve added elements across the promenade to enhance its charm and appeal but it could do with some regular and serious maintenance & upkeep.

Also a majority of pet peeps who regularly walk their dogs out here aren’t too big on leashes ( you can choose to do with this information / opinion as you like). Great spot to interact with doggos.

A few people have pointed out that the dog park isn’t exactly the best or safe environment for dogs to play on account of them encountering some health issues on odd occasions.

featured_reviews.name: Shakeel Ahmed
featured_reviews.review_text:
This 1.5 km long promenede along the black stone beaches of Khar-Danda shores is a very good place for walkers n joggers, not for runners.

Along the long narrow promenede, you see famous mangroves reserved forest, gym, dogs park, kids park, skating rink, koli (sea) food corner n wider sitting space overseeing beautiful view of sea n under construction Carter connector to upcoming Versova-Bandra Sea Link (VBSL) coastal road project.

Towards the North, u can smell drying fish odour ( ;>) coming from Danda Koliwada n morning releiving scenes.

Towards the South, if you cross under construction Carter bridge, you reach to Joggers Park which is separately reviewed.

A latest edition to this Promenade is sea food eatery stalls made at the North end at Khar Danda. Run by local fishermen community women, their classic savours are worth challenging Khau Galli costly restraurants opposite side.

See review of "Khar Danda Koli Savour" also.

review_photos.caption: Sea-food festival at every Friday-Saturday-Sunday at this end of promenade. Koli savours.

featured_reviews.name: Sharad Khandelwal
featured_reviews.review_text:
Its just so peaceful and serene to have a walk here. We decided to spent some us time bere on New Years instead of crowded places and it was a bliss!
There are ample places to sit and enjoy the sunset and the sea. There's a park for kids along with a dog park too!
Its just mesmerizing to see the sunset here and spent time with your loved ones and friends. Or just plain and simple have a hearty walk alongside the sea!

featured_reviews.name: Advocate Rita Kapur
featured_reviews.review_text:
It's a delight for early morning walkers to see hundreds of school  kids every Sunday morning happily  doing their studies along  the Carter road seaside  promenade.  Kids are helped for any difficulties they face in their studies and are made to understand the importance & need for education and self-sufficiency. Children are also served  breakfast  thereafter.  This initiative is of the NGO NAVJYOT in Mumbai and is personally overseen by  senior decades long dedicated women volunteers who are there on the spot  every Sunday morn.
Some photos of these happy kids facing the amazing Arabian Sea. An eye opener for sure.

featured_reviews.name: Soham Parekh
featured_reviews.review_text: This place is a must visit, especially if you're a couple. It's approximately 1-1.5 km long street by the sea, perpendicular to it is a row of cafés. It has a lot of benches, just by the sea, where you can sit and enjoy the beauty of the sea. It's moderately crowded and often has policeman standing guard. Pick something up to drink and munch on from the cafe and sit by the sea on one of the benches and enjoy the sunset. You'll thank me for the wonderful time you'll have. There's one particular bench right on the rocks which is just perfect, if you can find it, you'll enjoy it even more.

featured_reviews.name: Indra Pal Singh
featured_reviews.review_text:
Construction: Built by the British East India Company between 1669 and 1677 under Governor Gerald Aungier, it served as a lookout point.
Strategic Location: It marked the boundary between the British-controlled Parel Island and the Portuguese-held Salsette Island.
Remains: Visitors can find parts of the fort walls, parapets, a tank, and a cannon.
Views: The fort offers excellent views of the surrounding city, including modern skyscrapers, despite its fragmented state.
Visiting Information
Location: Sion East, near Sion Railway Station.
Entry: Free.
Best Time to Visit: November to February (pleasant weather) or during monsoons.
Vibe: A peaceful spot for history buffs, photographers, and couples, often described as a hidden gem.
What to Expect
A climb up a hill to reach the fort.
A mix of historical ruins and natural greenery.

featured_reviews.name: RuSo
featured_reviews.review_text: Sion Fort is a small but historically important spot tucked away in the busy heart of Mumbai. Built by the British in the 17th century, the fort sits on a hillock and once served as a watchtower to keep an eye on the surrounding areas. Today, it has been converted into a peaceful garden maintained by the BMC, making it a nice place for a short walk or some quiet time away from traffic and crowds. The fort structure itself is quite simple and not very well preserved, but the greenery and calm atmosphere make it pleasant to visit. It’s ideal for locals, morning walkers, and history enthusiasts looking for a quick, relaxed stop rather than a major tourist attraction.

featured_reviews.name: shailesh kathirvel
featured_reviews.review_text: Sion Fort is a peaceful little escape in the middle of the city. The climb is easy and takes just a few minutes, and once you reach the top, the view of Sion and the surrounding areas is really refreshing. It’s a great spot for a quick morning or evening visit, especially if you enjoy calm places and a bit of history. The fort is simple but well maintained, and the greenery around adds to the charm. A nice place to relax, walk around, and enjoy the breeze.

featured_reviews.name: INDERJIT BARAI
featured_reviews.review_text:
Sion Fort is a beautiful historical monument with great potential, but unfortunately, its condition has deteriorated due to irresponsible behavior by some visitors. The structure itself is impressive, and the fort still carries a strong historical charm with its old walls, arches, and scenic surroundings. If properly cared for, it could be an excellent heritage spot in the city.

However, the experience is spoiled by the actions of people who do not respect the monument. Names are scribbled on the walls, which damages the heritage value of the fort. It is also disturbing to see small boys around 8–10 years old smoking and using vapes inside the premises. Some reckless visitors pluck flowers and even climb on the fort walls, which are already weak and not in a safe condition. Such activities not only harm the monument but also put lives at risk. Overall, Sion Fort is a very good monument, but stricter rules, better maintenance, and public awareness are urgently needed to protect it for future generations.

featured_reviews.name: Learn 'To be smart
featured_reviews.review_text: Shiv Fort is a historical monument located in Sion, Mumbai. It is a good place to visit if you are interested in history, culture, and nature. The fort is situated on a hill, so you will have to climb many stairs to reach the top. The management is good and the stairs are well-maintained, but be prepared to get tired. There are different types of things you can buy on the way, such as souvenirs, snacks, and drinks. The view from the top is amazing, especially during sunset. You can take some awesome pictures and enjoy the scenery. However, there is not much to do on the top, so you might get bored if you do not bring enough food and entertainment. There is a park nearby for children, where they can play on the swings and other rides. To reach Shiv Fort, you can take a train to Sion station and then walk straight for about 600 meters. You will find the fort on the left side of the road. Overall, Shiv Fort is a nice place to visit for a day trip, but not very exciting if you are looking for more adventure.
